candidate.answerReason: B is the midpoint of AE. If angle ACE is right, the median BC to hypotenuse AE has length AE/2=AB, forcing equal adjacent sides AB and BC.

methods.label: Use the midpoint of the hypotenuse
methods.explanation:
Because \(AB\) is extended beyond \(B\) to \(E\) and \(AB=BE\), the point \(B\) is the midpoint of \(AE\). Thus \(BC\) is a median of triangle \(ACE\).

If \(\angle ACE=90^\circ\), then \(AE\) is the hypotenuse. In a right triangle, the median from the right-angle vertex to the hypotenuse has length half the hypotenuse. Therefore
\[
BC=\frac{AE}{2}=AB.
\]
The segments \(AB\) and \(BC\) are sides of quadrilateral \(ABCD\), so it must have at least one pair of equal sides. This is choice D. The necessary equality is specifically \(AB=BC\); an unspecified equal side pair alone would not guarantee the right angle.
